Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck and low back pain, muscle
tightness, and reduced range of motion. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the force of the clolision and with
the symptoms described. Cervical and lumbar paraspinal tenderness and restricted active motion were documented on
examination, while neurological screening, reflexes, and motor strength remained within normal limits. The patient has no known
prior injury or treatment involving the cervical or lumbar spine. Care was delivered over 21 visits, which is somewhat longer than
typical for uncomplicated cervical and lumbar strain, and included manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home exercise
instruction. Progress has been gradual, with improvement in pain scores and mobility over the course of treatment. Billed
services reviewed for this episode show no duplicated or repeated charges. Ongoing care will focus on strengthening and a
graded return to usual activities, with reassessment planned at discharge.
</page>
